title: Promptset throughput & regression exploration (latency / cost / quality)
content:
Summary:

This is a working note from the recent model-onboarding sweep focused on the tradeoffs between latency, token-level cost, and end-to-end quality for our candidate open models. The purpose: produce actionable thresholds that feeding into the onboarding checklist and the rollout/fallback policies in the Console.

Scope and motivation:
- Target models: small/medium open LLM family (7B/13B comparables) that teams want onboarded as lower-cost fallbacks.
- Workload: mixed promptset (QA + summarization + instruction following) derived from the onboarding prompt set repo (subset A: 1.2k prompts, 50/50 QA:summarize split).
- Hardware tested: A10G (prod Dedicated pool), H100-sim (dev harness w/ optimized kernels).
- Key knobs: request_batch_size (1, 4, 16, 64), KV cache enabled/disabled, max_tokens cap (64, 128, 512), quantization profiles (fp16, int8), and kernel selection (default vs packed-attn).
- Metrics collected: mean_latency_ms (per-request, end-to-end serve path), p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd (inferred using pricing model), and quality metrics (qa_exact_match, rouge_l, instruction_success_rate).

Experiment notes (methodology):
- Each sweep ran on consistent traffic emulator (1000 synthetic requests per experiment, uniform sampling from the 1.2k promptset).
- Warmup: 200 requests with KV prefill when cache enabled.
- For caching experiments we measured cache_hit_ratio and also tracked cold-start latency distribution separately.
- Cost model: used Dedicated per-token estimate for A10G from pricing table (0.0009 USD per 1k prompt tokens, 0.0042 USD per 1k completion tokens) plus an execution multiplier by measured GPU time, giving cost_per_1k_tokens_usd that aligns with internal billing projections.
- Quality: used the onboarding harness scoring (weighted aggregate: 0.5*qa_exact_match + 0.3*rouge_l_norm + 0.2*instr_success). We record absolute drop vs baseline (baseline = fp16, batch=1, cache on, max_tokens=512).

High-level findings (short):
- Batching dramatically improves tokens/sec and lowers per-token cost beyond batch=4, but p95 latency increases non-linearly after batch=16 for short prompts (QA).
- KV cache gives the best of both worlds for instruction-following and multi-turn prompts: cache on reduces mean_latency by ~22% and cost_per_1k_tokens by ~18% for workloads with prefix reuse, but it hurts cold-start QoS for single-shot prompts.
- Max_tokens cap at 128 cuts completion cost by ~35% with minimal quality degradation on QA prompts, but for summarization examples (longer targets) it introduces measurable rouge_l degradation (~6% relative).
- Int8 quantization reduces memory & enables larger batches on A10G but introduced a small quality drop (~1.8% on the weighted score); acceptable for low-tier fallback but not for primary serving in high-SLO customers.

Representative numeric slice (selected lines from aggregated CSV):
- Baseline (fp16, batch=1, cache=on, max=512): mean_latency_ms=220, p95_latency_ms=460, tokens_per_second=115, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd=0.92, quality_score=0.873
- Batch=4 (fp16, cache=on, max=512): mean_latency_ms=145, p95_latency_ms=320, tokens_per_second=320, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd=0.60, quality_score=0.871
- Batch=16 (fp16, cache=on, max=512): mean_latency_ms=210, p95_latency_ms=610, tokens_per_second=860, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd=0.28, quality_score=0.868
- Batch=16 + int8: mean_latency_ms=175, p95_latency_ms=540, tokens_per_second=1020, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd=0.19, quality_score=0.856
- Cache=off, batch=4, max=128: mean_latency_ms=165, p95_latency_ms=350, tokens_per_second=280, cost_per_1k_tokens_usd=0.44, quality_score=0.847

Interpretation and heuristics for onboarding:
1) For short-latency, high-SLO endpoints (chat-like QA), prefer batch <=4, cache enabled, max_tokens <=128. This keeps p95 < 400ms on A10G and preserves quality.
2) For throughput-first, non-interactive jobs (bulk embeddings/reranking style prompts), batch >=16 with int8 is cost-effective if the customer accepts a small quality delta.
3) Use cache on by default for multi-turn or prefix-heavy promptsets. Add a canary check for cold-start latency (requests following model restart or after cache invalidation).
4) Max_tokens should be set per-route: 128 default for short completion tasks; 512 only for known long-completion routes (summarization).

Observed regressions and red flags:
- One model variant (quantized 13B equivalent) showed a 4.7% drop in qa_exact_match when max_tokens was lowered from 512->128 for QA prompts that include long reference contexts. This indicates some tasks are sensitive to completion truncation in subtle ways (answer chopping, hallucination increase).
- p95 tail with batch=16 spiked on mixed-length workloads; root cause appears to be kernel scheduling interaction with packed-attn on A10G and the dev harness VMM fragmentation. Needs SRE/infra follow-up.
- Int8 variant occasionally produced malformed tokenization edges on a small set (~0.3%) of prompts (non-deterministic tokenization artifacts). Reproducible locally with quantization RNG seed fixed. Escalating to model-ops.

Checklist additions for onboarding playbook (proposed):
- Mandatory sweep: run batch=[1,4], cache=[on,off], max_tokens=[128,512] and collect the weighted_quality_score + mean & p95 latencies. If weighted_quality_score < baseline - 2% and p95 > target_SLO then fail onboarding.
- Regression tests: include the 120 prompt regression set (subset A stable) and track qa_exact_match and rouge_l; add automated alert if qa_exact_match drops >=3% vs model family baseline.
- Cold-start check: simulate model restart and measure first 50 requests latency and cache_hit_ratio; require p95_cold < 1.5x steady_p95 for interactive routes.
- Quantization policy: tag quantized builds as "low_tier" and require an explicit business sign-off before enabling for customer-facing default routes.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add a latency budget field to the onboarding metadata that maps to recommended batch/cache/max_tokens? (I think yes; easiest place to feed into the Console autosuggest.)
- How should we encode prefix/cache heuristics per-route when user prompts are opaque (no schema)? Propose: allow customers to declare expected prefix_reuse_rate and provide an inference-safe default.
- Need infra ticket to investigate packed-attn scheduling with mixed-length batches on A10G (see linked PR).

Action items (owners):
- Ravi: file infra follow-up for p95 tail (JIRA-ML-3427) and add perf trace hooks to packed-attn kernel (due 2026-03-12).
- Sofia: expand the onboarding regression set with 200 more edge-case prompts from CS reductions and rerun sweep with updated quantization codepath (due 2026-03-10).
- Me (Maya): draft a short Console UX proposal to add "latency budget" and per-route recommended knobs; share with Product and DevX by 2026-03-08.

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- We should capture a short example in the onboarding UI: e.g., "If you need p95 < 400ms, we suggest batch <=4 + cache on + max_tokens=128 (A10G)." Concrete suggestions make the default less magical.
- Consider a small cost-sensitivity experiment that ties real customer traffic patterns to cost_per_1k_tokens_usd to validate the billing projection model above.

Attachments / where results are stored:
- Aggregated CSVs and raw traces: s3://redwood-inference-experiments/onboarding/2026-02-latency-cost-sweep/
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-evals (branch: rapid-latency-sweep)

If you're reviewing: please call out anything that looks like an unacceptable quality regression (particularly around QA exact match) or any other test you'd like added to the mandatory sweep.
